name: Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia with HOXA11 Mutation
aliases: Inherited Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia due to HOXA11

criteria.description: Persistent severe thrombocytopenia present from birth or early infancy
Bone marrow examination showing marked reduction or absence of megakaryocytes
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the HOXA11 gene
Exclusion of other inherited or acquired causes of thrombocytopenia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent thrombocytopenia with bone marrow amegakaryocytosis and confirmed HOXA11 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; bone marrow biopsy is critical to exclude other causes.

laboratory: Severe thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically <20,000/µL
Normal or reduced white blood cell and red blood cell counts in advanced cases
Bone marrow biopsy showing absent or markedly reduced megakaryocytes
imaging: Skeletal survey may reveal limb abnormalities in rare cases
other: Exclusion of other inherited thrombocytopenias and acquired causes is essential

distinguishingFeatures: Mutation in MPL gene instead of HOXA11
Similar bone marrow findings but different genetic cause

redFlags: Severe bleeding in neonate or early infancy
Progressive pancytopenia indicating bone marrow failure
Family history of early-onset thrombocytopenia or bone marrow failure
references: Ballmaier M, Germeshausen M. Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia: clinical and molecular aspects. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2009;2009(1):160-166.
Vainchenker W, et al. Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia: molecular basis and clinical implications. Haematologica. 2016;101(6):660-670.
